newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB to split operations into three units.
newsitem.headline: NCB to split operations into three units.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Wednesday that it would split its operations into three separate units in a bid to boost efficiency and focus on specialised areas.
The bank said in a statement that the split-up would take effect on September 1.
An NCB spokesman said the move was not a prelude to the formation of a financial holding company, adding that details about a financial holding company have not been decided yet.

The three units include a banking unit focusing on the securitisation of assets and other banking-related businesses, a financial unit focusing on risk and asset management, and a project promotion unit focusing on recovering problem loans and on real estate transactions, it said.

In April, NCB announced a sweeping restructuring plan, including a withdrawal from overseas operations and a termination of financial support to troubled non-bank financial affiliates. The plan aims to boost profits by 50 billion yen over the next five years.
NCB hopes to position itself as a specialised bank, with a goal of 10 trillion yen in total assets and 2,000 employees.
